title: Changing an item in place
idea: Introduce item assignment: list[i] = value replaces the item at a position. Visible output; uses indexing from Unit 52.

exercises.prompt: To CHANGE the item at a position, you put the indexed spot on the left of = and the new value on the right. Which line changes the first item of n to 99?
exercises.explanation: n[0] = 99 replaces the item at position 0 with 99. It's like a variable assignment, but aimed at one spot in the list.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

n = [10, 20, 30]
n[1] = 99
print(n)
exercises.explanation: Position 1 is the second item, 20. Assigning n[1] = 99 replaces it, giving [10, 99, 30]. Length is unchanged.

exercises.prompt: Changing an item with list[i] = value keeps the list the same length.
exercises.explanation: You replaced one value in an existing spot. No item was added or removed, so the count stays the same.

exercises.prompt: How is n[1] = 99 different from n.append(99)?
options: Assignment replaces an existing item; append adds a new one at the end
Assignment adds an item; append replaces one
exercises.explanation: Assignment changes a spot that's already there (same length). append grows the list by one. Two different jobs.

exercises.prompt:
Change the LAST item to 0. Fill in the position:

n = [5, 6, 7]
n[____] = 0
print(n)
exercises.explanation: n[-1] = 0 (or n[2] = 0) targets the last spot, giving [5, 6, 0]. You can assign to any valid position, even -1.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output:

scores = [70, 80, 90]
scores[0] = scores[0] + 5
print(scores)
exercises.explanation: scores[0] is 70; 70 + 5 is 75; assigning puts 75 back in spot 0. You can use the old value to compute the new one.

exercises.prompt: You can only assign to a position that already exists in the list.
exercises.explanation: Assignment replaces an EXISTING item. To put something at a brand-new spot past the end, you append instead.

exercises.prompt: Arrange tokens to change the item at position 2 of a list named row to 50.
exercises.explanation: row[2] = 50 replaces the third item with 50. Indexed spot on the left of =, new value on the right.

exercises.prompt: A list has 3 items. A learner writes n[3] = 100 to add a fourth. Why does it fail?
options: Position 3 doesn't exist yet — assignment can't create a new spot; use append
exercises.explanation: Three items fill positions 0, 1, 2. There's no position 3 to assign to. To add a new item, use n.append(100).

exercises.prompt: What new tool did this lesson add?
options: A way to make a list
exercises.explanation: list[i] = value replaces the item at a position in place. Together with append, you can now grow and change lists.
